Maria G.: Quick proposal draft — we should introduce a soft-cap window + overflow guard for free/pro customers to avoid noisy-neighbor storms and sudden bill spikes. Idea: softcap per-org that starts signalling at 80% of the plan bandwidth for a rolling 1m window, allow bursts up to 150% for a short burst budget, then apply gentle token-throttles instead of hard rejects.

Jon P.: I like signalling. Can you sketch enforcement semantics? e.g., is it per-key or per-org first?

Maria G.: Per-org first (so teams can manage), falling back to per-key when org-level attribution missing. Enforcement steps: 1) Emit event at 80% (telemetry + console warning). 2) Allow bursts up to burst_budget tokens over 60s. 3) If sustained above 150% for 2m, apply smoothing: limit to steady rate = plan_rate * 1.0 and degrade burst headroom. 4) Only hard limit (429) when we hit emergency cap (300% sustained 3m) or abuse flags.

Ashok N.: What's the burst_budget unit? tokens or request-count? We need to align with billing units (tokens) or else observability is confusing.

Maria G.: tokens. Example: Free plan = 10k tokens/min baseline. Softcap triggers at 8k, burst_budget = 5k over 60s (so can reach 13k briefly), emergency at sustained >30k. Numbers are placeholders.

Emily R.: UX question: console should show "softcap warnings" on org dashboard and per-key detail. Also add a time-series for burst budget left so product teams know when they're draining it.

Kevin S.: Telemetry needs: emit metrics: quota_usage_tokens, softcap_flag (bool), burst_budget_remaining, enforcement_state (green/yellow/red), enforcement_action (none/smoothing/throttle/hard_reject). We can wire that into existing per-route dashboards.

Jon P.: How do we handle Dedicated customers? They expect no silent throttles. Maybe opt-out if Dedicated or Enterprise contract clause?

Maria G.: Yes — Dedicated/Enterprise get opt-out or custom SLA. Default softcap applies to Hosted free/pro. For Dedicated, we still recommend signals but no automatic throttles unless explicitly enabled.

Ashok N.: Implementation sketch in edge-proxy: maintain leaky-bucket per-org with two thresholds. When usage enters soft window, emit an annotation to request headers (x-quota-state) so downstream can log. For enforcement, use adaptive token-bucket that reduces refill rate progressively.

Maria G.: Example config snippet: 
```
plan: free
baseline_rate: 10000 # tokens/min
soft_threshold: 0.8
burst_budget: 5000 # tokens per 60s
burst_window: 60s
emergency_multiplier: 3.0
```

QuotaBot: [automated] New proposal created: softcap-overflow-guardrails (RFC-2026). Link: https://rwg/internal/rfcs/2026 :thumbsup:

Emily R.: For rollout: feature-flag the enforcement (gradual). Step 1: telemetry-only for 2 weeks; Step 2: notify on console + email to org admins when softcap triggers; Step 3: enable smoothing for 10% of orgs as canary; Step 4: global enable.

Kevin S.: We should also show estimated cost impact: if a free org consistently uses >baseline, suggest upgrade to Pro with projected delta and a one-click plan change from console.

Ashok N.: Edge case: bursty inference workloads where short-lived peaks are normal (e.g., batch jobs). We should allow white-listing of scheduled jobs or support a "scheduled-burst" token that can be pre-reserved via API.

Jon P.: Agree. Also need API for customers to query burst_budget_remaining and softcap_window so they can gracefully backoff client-side. Add endpoints: GET /quota/status and webhook for softcap events.

Maria G.: Action items: 
- Ashok: prototype leaky-bucket + adaptive refill in edge proxy (P0) — due Tue next week.
- Kevin: add metrics definitions & dashboard wireframe (P1) — due Fri.
- Emily: console UX for warnings + upgrade CTA (P1) — due Fri.
- Jon: API surface for /quota/status + webhooks (P1) — due Mon.
- I'll draft RFC and number ranges for free/pro/enterprise (P0) — due tomorrow.

Jon P.: One more: audit log entry on any enforcement action for compliance.

Maria G.: Good call. Add to spec.

Kevin S.: tagging ops: @ops-team please review telemetry cost implications (high-card metrics?)

QuotaBot: [automated] Assigned: Ashok N., Kevin S., Emily R., Jon P., Maria G.

Emily R.: Thanks all — will sync up after prototypes. :rocket:
